- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1-2% to prevent overcorrection lag.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in the 10-15 day horizon; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the 10-15 day window if sentiment is bullish.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
